title: Lens Operations
description: Lithos Lens: the Lithos call funnel, event hub, admission control and knowledge surface. Panels are organised by failure mode rather than by route.

panels.description:
1 while the MCP tool session is established. `min` across the selected environments, so any instance being down shows down. This is the TOOL session, not the event stream — the two connect separately and can disagree.

No data means no lens instance is reporting at all.
panels.title: Lithos MCP Session

panels.description: 1 while the Lithos `/events` SSE stream is live. A board that renders but never updates is this reading 0 while the MCP session reads 1.
panels.title: Event Stream

panels.description: Lithos MCP call rate over 15m. Lens polls on a timer, so a healthy idle lens still shows steady background traffic — a drop to zero here with the session up means the poll loop has stopped.
panels.title: Tool Calls / min

panels.description:
Non-`ok` outcomes: timeout, tool_error, transport_error, cancelled.

`or vector(0)` is deliberate — a counter that has never fired has no series, so without it a perfectly healthy lens would read *No data* here, indistinguishable from broken instrumentation.
panels.title: Tool Failures / min

panels.description: 95th percentile Lithos call latency over 15m, queue time included. The red threshold is CALL_TIMEOUT_S (15s) — at that point calls are being abandoned rather than served.
panels.title: Tool Call p95

panels.description: 95th percentile time blocked at the process-wide call gate. This is the signal that separates *Lithos is slow* from *lens is admitting more concurrent work than it can pass through* — both otherwise present identically, as slow pages.
panels.title: Queue Wait p95

panels.description: Every lens client method funnels through `MCPTransport.call_tool`, so this covers the whole client surface. `tool` is a bounded set — lens's own methods, roughly twenty.
panels.title: Call Rate by Tool

panels.description: The failure taxonomy, kept apart because each calls for a different response: `timeout` means LENS gave up (look at load or the deadline), `tool_error` means Lithos said no, `transport_error` means the socket failed, `cancelled` means the caller went away.
panels.title: Call Outcomes

panels.description: End-to-end call latency, queue time included — a queued call has not answered yet. Split it against Queue Wait below to see which half is slow.
panels.title: Tool Call Duration

panels.description: `acquired=false` is the waiting time of a call that was SHED rather than served — the deadline spans the queue, so a caller can time out while still waiting. Recording only successful acquires would leave this quiet at exactly the moment queueing was doing all the damage.
panels.title: Queue Wait by Outcome

panels.description: The two connections plus the reconnect rate. A session that reads `up` while reconnecting every minute is not healthy — the gauge alone cannot show that, which is why the rate is on the right-hand axis here.
panels.title: Session Health & Reconnects

panels.description: Which Lithos tools dominate lens's latency budget. Use for postmortems and for deciding what to cache.
panels.title: Slowest Tools p95 (1h)

panels.description: Events accepted from upstream (by type) against per-subscriber deliveries. `type` is mapped through an allowlist at the recording site, not taken from the event — fake-Lithos mode exposes a publish endpoint that builds events straight from request JSON, so trusting it would let a request mint arbitrary Prometheus series.
panels.title: Publish & Delivery Rate

panels.description:
SSE subscribers attached to the hub, read from the authoritative `len(subscribers)` at collection time, so it cannot drift after a missed unsubscribe. The dashed line is MAX_EVENT_SUBSCRIBERS (128); past it lens answers 503.

`max` across instances, NOT `sum`: the ceiling is enforced per EventHub, so two healthy replicas holding 70 each would sum to 140 and render red while neither is anywhere near refusing. The worst single instance is the one that starts answering 503.
panels.title: Subscribers vs Ceiling

panels.description:
The five conditions the rate-limited warnings report. The log line keeps the human-readable detail; this carries the RATE, which the rate limiter necessarily discards — correctly, since a misbehaving upstream must not get to choose how fast lens writes to the operator's log.

Empty here means nothing has been dropped: a counter with no increments has no series. The stat below reads 0 explicitly.
panels.title: Drops by Reason

panels.description: Deliveries per published event over 1h. This is the number that decides whether the subscriber ceiling is close to mattering.
panels.title: Fan-out per Event

panels.description: Total events refused or discarded in the last hour, across all reasons. Reads 0 rather than *No data* when healthy.
panels.title: Drops (1h)

panels.description: Cumulative event mix. Types outside the allowlist collapse into `other`.
panels.title: Events Published by Type (total)

panels.description: Metered requests at the render semaphore. Refusals are otherwise visible only as users receiving 503s.
panels.title: Admissions by Outcome

panels.description:
From the FastAPI instrumentation, which returns before touching this counter for anything in `excluded_urls` — so `/health`, `/static` and the `/tasks/events` SSE stream are ABSENT from it. That makes it a close proxy for metered concurrency rather than raw connection count, and in particular a browser tab holding an SSE stream open for hours does not sit in this number. The dashed line is MAX_CONCURRENT_RENDERS (128).

`max` per instance, not a sum across them: the semaphore is per process, so summing replicas would compare a fleet total against a per-process limit.
panels.title: Requests In Flight

panels.description: `http_target` is the route TEMPLATE (`/note/{knowledge_id}`), never the concrete path — ids would otherwise mint a series each. Requests that match no route carry no `http_target` at all, so scanner traffic collapses into a single unlabelled series instead of one per probed URL.
panels.title: Request Rate by Route

panels.description: Server-side p95 per route. Compare against Tool Call Duration: a route slow while its Lithos calls are fast is lens's own rendering, not the backend.
panels.title: Route Latency p95

panels.description: Status distribution. A rising 404 rate with no matching route is usually scanner noise; 503s are admission refusals or the subscriber ceiling.
panels.title: HTTP Status Mix

panels.description: `not_found` is kept apart from `error` because they are different problems wearing the same 200: a dead wiki-link someone should fix, versus Lithos failing to answer.
panels.title: Note Renders by Outcome

panels.description: The expensive half of a note render — one `lithos_related` call plus a bounded `lithos_read` fan-out. Also a named child span (`lens.knowledge.related`), so a slow panel can be opened in Tempo.
panels.title: Related Panel Duration

panels.description: Backend reads spent resolving related-panel titles. The dashed line is the default `related_title_fanout_cap` (20). A p95 sitting ON the cap means notes are being silently truncated; one far below it means the cap costs nothing and the latency is elsewhere.
panels.title: Related Fan-out vs Cap

panels.description: `search` is a hybrid `lithos_search`; `browse` is the recency list. The raw query is deliberately absent from this label — one series per distinct search is unbounded cardinality driven by unauthenticated input. It IS on the span, where it costs no series.
panels.title: Searches by Mode

panels.description: Which arm decided. A corpus resolving entirely by `uuid` is working for a different reason than one resolving by `title`, and only the second is evidence the wiki-link convention is being used as intended.
panels.title: Wiki-link Resolutions by Arm

panels.description:
`unresolved` as a share of all resolutions. A rising share is the corpus growing dead links — a content problem, not an availability one.

Under-reports for the first day after a restart: `increase()` cannot see a counter's first increment, because the series appears already holding that value.
panels.title: Dead-link Share (24h)

panels.description: Cumulative resolution mix.
panels.title: Resolutions by Arm (total)

panels.description: Lens's JSON logs, health-check and static noise filtered. Every line logged inside a request carries `traceid` / `spanid`, and the Loki datasource turns those into a View Trace link into Tempo — so a warning here opens the trace it came from.
panels.title: Lens Logs (trace-linked)
